analysis:
Reconciled the supplied local analysis with the replayed patches, metadata and source excerpts. docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md head lines 3 and 65 update the date and document retaining a complete field/chunk read without copying it into another buffer. changelog.d/ssd-read-single-copy.md head lines 3–8 describe that optimization and a debug-build benchmark, not production qualification. The supplied changes do not visibly alter authentication, cache scope, HMAC naming, AES-GCM/AAD, TTL, purge policy or path protections relevant to A-001, TB-007 and T-041. No changes to provider authorization, attestation, wire encryption, billing, privileged helpers or installer execution are evidenced. No concrete regression or material threat-model change is independently supported by these documentation changes.
The remaining local question cannot be resolved from this integration evidence: provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/KVCacheSSD/SSDBlockStore.swift readExactly and its consumers are not supplied. Review the implementation's complete-read fast path and short-read fallback for exact-length/EOF handling, bounded allocation, pre-read budget accounting and buffer ownership through authentication/decryption; verify interaction with SSDBlockChunkCursor and streaming/checkpoint readers. Those contracts matter under adversarial provider-controlled storage, but their absence here is not evidence of missing controls. The replay omits two previously reviewed units, so the local analysis's surrounding-source claims cannot all be directly rechecked. Further review is needed for the stated implementation optimization, not for an observed documentation vulnerability.
